source_text: 1. Quon1am igitur in hoe mundo quidam quidem accurrunt lumini, et per fidem uniunt se Deo; alii autem absistunt a lumine, et separant seipsos a Deo: venit Verbum Dei, omnibus aptam habitationem inferens ; his quidem qui in lumine sunt, ut fruantur eo, et his quee in eo sunt bonis: his autem qui in tenebris sunt, ut participentur eas calamitates quze in eis sunt. Et propter hoe ait, hos quidem qui sunt ad dexteram vocari in regnum Patris: autem qui sunt a sinistra in eternum ignem missurum, Semetipsos enim omnibus privaverunt bonis, 2. Et propter hoe Apostolus ait: Pro eo quod dilectionem Dei non receperunt, ut salvi ferent, et ideo mittet eis Deus operationem erroris, ut credant mendacio, ut judicentur omnes qui non crediderunt veritati, sed consenserunt iniquitati : illo enim veniente, et sua sententia apostasiam recapitulante in semetipsum, et sua voluntate et arbitrio operante quaecunque operabitur, et in templo Dei sedente, ut sicut Christum adorent illum qui seducentur ab quapropter et juste in stagnum projicietur ignis ; Deo autem secundum suam providentiam preesciente omnia, et apto tempore eum qui talis futurus erat immittente, wt credant falso, ut judicentur omnes qui non crediderunt veritati, sed consenserunt iniquitati. Cujus adventum Johannes in Apocalypsi significavit ita: Et bestia quam videram, similis erat pardo, et pedes ejus quasi ursi, et os ejus quasi os leonis; et dedit ei draco virtutem suam, et thronum suum, et potestatem magnam; et unum ew capitibus ejus’ quasi occisum in mortem, e plaga mortis ejus curata est, et admirata est universa terra post bestiam: et adoraverunt draconem, 4 quoniam dedit potestatem bestie ; et adoraverunt bestiam dicentes: Quis similis bestice illi, et quis potest pugnare cum ipsa? Et datum est e os loquens magna et blasphemiam, et data est ei potestas mensibus xu. et ®duobus. Et aperuit os swum ad blasphemium adversus Deum, blasphemare nomen ejus, et tabernaculum ejus, et eos qui in colo habitant, Ht data est ei potestas super omnem tribum, et populum, et linguam, et gentem. Et adoraverunt eum omnes qui habitant super terram, cujus non est scriptum nomen in libro vitee Agni occisi a constitutione mundi. Si quis habet aures, audiat. Si quis in captivitatem duxerit, in captivitatem ibit. Si quis gladio occioportet eum in gladio occidi. Hic est sustinentia et fides sanctorum. Post deinde et de armigero ejus, quem et pseudoprophetam vocat : Loguebatur, inquit, quasi draco, et potestatem prime bestice omnem faciebat in conspectu aus : et facit terram, et qui habitant in ea, ut adorarent bestiam primam, cujus curata est plaga mortis ejus. Et faciet signa magna, ut e ignem faciat de celo descendere in terram in conspectu hominum ; et seducet inhabitantes super terram, Heee ne quis eum divina virtute putet signa facere, sed magica operatione. Et non est mirandum, si deemoniis et apostaticis spiritibus ministrantibus ei, per eos faciat signa, in seducat habitantes super terram. Et imaginem, ait, Jubebit fiers bestiae, et spiritum dabit imagini, uti et loquatur imago, et eos qui non adoraverint eam faciet occidi. Et characterem autem, ait, in fronte, et in manu dextra faciet dari, ne possit aliquis emere vel vendere, nisi qui habet characterem nominis bestia, vel numerum nominis ejus: et esse numerum sexcentos sexaginta sew, quod est, sexies centeni, et deni sewies, et singulares sex; im universze apostasize ejus, quze facta est in sex millibus annorum. 8. Quotquot enim diebus hic factus est mundus, tot et millenis annis consummatur. Et propter hoe ait Scriptura Et consummata sunt celum et terra, et omnis ornatus ecorum. consummavit Deus die sexto omnia opera sua que fecit, et requievit in die septimo ab omnibus operibus suis que fecit. Hoe autem est et antefactorum narratio, quemadmodum facta sunt, et futurorum prophetia. Etenim dies Domini quasi mille anni; in sex autem diebus consummata sunt que facta sunt: manifestum est quoniam consummatio ipsorum sextus millesimus annus est. Et propter hoc in omni tempore, plasmatus initio homo per manus Dei, id est, Filii et Spiritus, fit secundum imaginem et similitudinem Dei, paleis quidem abjectis, quee sunt apostasia ; frumento autem in horreum assumto, quod est hi qui ad Deum fide fructificant. Et propterea tribulatio necessaria est his qui salvantur, ut quodammodo contriti, et attenuati, et conspersi per patientiam Verbo Dei, et igniti, apti sint ad convivium Regis. Quemadmodum quidam de nostris dixit, propter martyrium in Deum adjudicatus ad bestias: Quoniam frumentum sum Christi, et per dentes bestiarum molor, ut mundus panis Dei inveniar. Universa ad utilitatem hominum facta esse: et de Antichristi dolis, nequitia, vi apostatica a diluvio, et deinceps in Ananie, Azarie et Misaelis persecutione, prafigurata.
thought_title: The Coming of the Word of God
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, since in this world some people indeed run to the light and through faith unite themselves to God, but others withdraw from the light and separate themselves from God: the Word of God comes, bringing a suitable dwelling for all; for those who are in the light, so that they may enjoy it and the good things that are in it; but for those who are in darkness, so that they may participate in the calamities that are in them. And because of this, it says that those who are on the right are called into the kingdom of the Father, but those who are on the left are sent into eternal fire. For they have deprived themselves of all good things. And because of this, the Apostle says: Since they did not receive the love of God, so that they might be saved, and therefore God will send them a working of error, so that they may believe a lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged. For when he comes, and with his own judgment recapitulates the apostasy in himself, and with his own will and decision operates whatever he operates, and sits in the temple of God, so that those who are seduced may adore him as if he were Christ; therefore, he will be justly thrown into the lake of fire. But God, according to his own providence, foreknowing all things, and at the suitable time sending him who was to be such, so that they may believe a lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged. The coming of whom John signified in the Apocalypse, saying: And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth was like the mouth of a lion; and the dragon gave it his power and his throne and great authority; and one of its heads was as if slain to death, and the wound of its death was healed, and the whole earth was amazed after the beast; and they worshiped the dragon, because he gave authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying: Who is like the beast, and who can fight against it? And it was given to it a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and authority was given to it for forty-two months. And it opened its mouth to blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name and his tabernacle and those who dwell in heaven. And authority was given to it over every tribe and people and language and nation. And all who dwell on the earth worshiped it, whose name is not written in the book of life of the slain Lamb from the foundation of the world. If anyone has ears, let him hear. If anyone is to be taken captive, to captivity he will go. If anyone is to be slain with the sword, with the sword he will be slain. This is the patience and faith of the saints. After this, also about his armor-bearer, whom he also calls a false prophet: He spoke, he says, like a dragon, and he performed all the power of the first beast in the sight of men; and he makes the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose wound of death was healed. And he will perform great signs, so that he even makes fire come down from heaven to earth in the sight of men; and he will seduce the inhabitants of the earth, so that they do not think that he performs signs by divine power, but by magical operation. And it is not to be wondered at, if he performs signs through demons and apostate spirits ministering to him, and seduces the inhabitants of the earth. And an image, he says, he will make of the beast, and he will give breath to the image, so that the image may even speak, and he will cause those who do not worship it to be slain. And a mark, he says, will be given on the forehead and on the right hand, so that no one may buy or sell except him who has the mark of the name of the beast or the number of his name; and the number is six hundred sixty-six, which is six times one hundred, and ten, and seven, and six; in all the apostasy that was made in six thousand years. For as many days as the world was made, so many thousand years it will be completed. And because of this, Scripture says: And the heaven and the earth and all their adornment were completed. God completed all his works that he made on the sixth day, and he rested on the seventh day from all his works that he made. But this is also a narrative of what has been done, and a prophecy of what will be. For the day of the Lord is like a thousand years; and in six days what has been done is completed; it is clear that the completion of these things is the sixth thousandth year. And because of this, in all time, man, formed at the beginning by the hands of God, that is, by the Son and the Spirit, is made according to the image and likeness of God, casting away the chaff, which is apostasy; but gathering the wheat into the storehouse, which is those who bear fruit in faith to God. And therefore, tribulation is necessary for those who are saved, so that, being somehow broken and attenuated and sprinkled through patience with the Word of God, and ignited, they may be fit for the banquet of the King. As one of ours said, who was condemned to the beasts for the testimony of God: For I am the grain of Christ, and I am ground by the teeth of the beasts, so that I may be found as the pure bread of God. All things were made for the utility of men; and about the snares of the Antichrist, and his wickedness, and his apostate power from the flood, and from then on in the persecution of Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, prefigured.

pass_b_english: In this world some people run toward the light and, by faith, bind themselves to God; others turn away from the light and cut themselves off from him. The Word of God therefore comes, bringing a fitting dwelling for everyone: for those in the light, that they may enjoy it and the good things within it; for those in darkness, that they may share in the calamities that already fill them. Because of this the text says that those on the right are summoned into the Father's kingdom, while those on the left are dispatched to eternal fire, for they have stripped themselves of every good.

The Apostle also declares: Because they refused to welcome the love of God that brings salvation, God will send them a powerful delusion so that they believe the lie, and so that all who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in wickedness may be judged. When this one arrives, he will gather the whole apostasy into himself by his own sentence, and by his own will and choice he will do whatever he pleases, seating himself in God's temple so that the deceived worship him as if he were Christ. For that reason he will be justly flung into the lake of fire. Yet God, in his providence, foreknew everything and at the appointed time sent the one destined to be such a figure, so that they would believe the lie and all who refused the truth and embraced iniquity would be condemned.

John foretold his coming in the Revelation: "The beast I saw resembled a leopard, its feet were like a bear's, its mouth like a lion's. The dragon gave the beast his power, his throne, and great authority. One of its heads seemed to have been slain, yet its fatal wound was healed, and the whole world marveled and followed the beast. They worshiped the dragon because he had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, 'Who is like the beast? Who can wage war against it?' The beast was given a mouth to utter proud words and blasphemies and authority to act for forty-two months. It opened its mouth to blaspheme God, to slander his name and his dwelling place and those who live in heaven. It was granted authority over every tribe, people, language, and nation. All inhabitants of the earth will worship it—everyone whose name has not been written in the Lamb's book of life, the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world. Let the one who has ears hear. If anyone is destined for captivity, into captivity they go; if anyone is destined to be killed by the sword, by the sword they will be killed. This calls for patient endurance and faithfulness on the part of the saints." (Rev 13:1–10; 2 Thess 2:9–12)

Then John speaks of the beast's lieutenant, the false prophet: "He spoke like a dragon and exercised all the authority of the first beast on its behalf, and made the earth and its inhabitants worship the first beast, whose fatal wound had been healed. He performed great signs, even calling down fire from heaven to earth in full view of the people. By these signs he deceived the inhabitants of the earth, telling them to make an image in honor of the beast that had been wounded by the sword yet lived. He was allowed to give breath to the image so that it could speak and cause all who refused to worship the image to be killed. He also forced everyone—small and great, rich and poor, free and slave—to receive a mark on the right hand or forehead, so that no one could buy or sell unless they had the mark, which is the name of the beast or the number of its name. This calls for wisdom: let the one who has insight calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and its number is 666." (Rev 13:11–18)

Six hundred sixty-six, then, is the sum of the whole apostasy that unfolded over six thousand years. As many days as were employed in creating the world, so many thousands of years will bring it to completion. That is why Scripture says: "Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array. By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing; so on the seventh day he rested from all his work." (Gen 1:1–2:25) This account of past events is simultaneously a prophecy of what is to come. A day of the Lord is like a thousand years; in six days the work was finished, so the consummation falls in the sixth millennium.

Throughout every age, the human being—formed at the beginning by the hands of God, that is, by the Son and the Spirit—is fashioned according to God's image and likeness. The chaff, which is apostasy, is discarded; the wheat, which is those who bear fruit in faith toward God, is gathered into the storehouse. Therefore tribulation is necessary for those who are being saved, so that, broken and refined and steeped in patience by the Word of God and set ablaze, they may become fit for the King's banquet. As one of our own said when he was condemned to the beasts for his witness to God: "I am Christ's wheat; I am ground by the teeth of beasts so that I may be found as pure bread for God." (Ps 90:4; Dan 3:1–30) All things were made for the benefit of humanity, and the treachery, wickedness, and apostate power of the Antichrist were prefigured from the flood onward, and again in the persecution of Ananias, Azarias, and Misael.
notes: The Latin text is from Irenaeus' Against Heresies 5.28

review.notes: Pass B adds significant content not present in the Locked Latin or Pass A, specifically regarding the mark of the beast. The Latin text says: 'ne possit aliquis emere vel vendere, nisi qui habet characterem nominis bestia, vel numerum nominis ejus' (so that no one may buy or sell except him who has the mark of the name of the beast or the number of his name). Pass B adds: 'He also forced everyone—small and great, rich and poor, free and slave—to receive a mark on the right hand or forehead'. The distinction of social classes (small and great, rich and poor, free and slave) is not in the source. Additionally, Pass B adds 'telling them to make an image in honor of the beast that had been wounded by the sword yet lived' which is a paraphrase/expansion of 'ut e ignem faciat de celo descendere in terram... et seducet inhabitantes super terram' and 'ut adorarent bestiam primam, cujus curata est plaga mortis ejus'.
reasons: Pass B adds 'small and great, rich and poor, free and slave' which is not in the Locked Latin 'ne possit aliquis emere vel vendere, nisi qui habet characterem nominis bestia, vel numerum nominis ejus'.
